**Date:** 2026-11-24 · **Tag:** `v6.1.0` · **Baseline:** `v6.0.0` · Security release

Install: `aztec-up install 6.1.0` · Docker: `azteclabs/aztec:6.1.0`

## Summary

> [!WARNING]
> **v6.1.0 is a security release. All Aztec nodes should upgrade as soon as possible.** It fixes a denial-of-service vulnerability in the node's JSON-RPC input handling. See [Security](#security).

This is a drop-in upgrade: no protocol change, same rollup, same data directory, and v6.1.0 runs alongside v6.0.0 nodes. Restart on the new image: `azteclabs/aztec:6.1.0`, or `aztec-up install 6.1.0`.

The only breaking change for operators affects custom `TX_PUBLIC_SETUP_ALLOWLIST` entries ([details](#breaking-changes)). Developers also have a few breaking changes, including Node.js 24.

## Update priority

| Who | Priority | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Nodes whose JSON-RPC port is reachable by untrusted clients | **High** | Upgrade first. Until you do, take the RPC port off the public internet. |
| Sequencers and validators | Medium | Upgrade. This release also fixes cases where honest validators could be reported for slashing. |
| Provers | Medium | Upgrade. If you set a `rolling:N` `WS_HISTORY_RETENTION`, check that it covers the proof submission window, or the node won't start. |
| Wallet and app developers | Medium | Move to the 6.1.0 packages and Node.js 24. See [Breaking changes](#breaking-changes). |

## Security

- **Denial of service through JSON-RPC input** ([#603](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/603), [#605](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/605), [#638](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/638), [#639](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/639)).
  - A crafted request to a node's JSON-RPC endpoint could make the node use excessive memory, or crash it.
  - v6.1.0 checks input sizes before parsing, and upgrades zod to 4.6.7 for [GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5).
  - Nodes whose JSON-RPC port is reachable by untrusted clients are affected. All other nodes should still upgrade.
  - **Action:** upgrade to v6.1.0. Until you do, keep the node's RPC port off the public internet.

## Breaking changes

**Node operators**

- **`TX_PUBLIC_SETUP_ALLOWLIST` is stricter, and static setup calls are rejected** ([#701](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/701)).
  - `cl=N`, like the new `l2=N` and `da=N` flags, accepts only a plain integer. `cl=4x` or `cl=1e3` used to be read as their leading digits; now the node fails to start with `Invalid allow list entry`.
  - A custom entry that targets a `#[view]` function no longer admits any transaction, so remove it.
  - Do not put `l2=` or `da=` in a network config that v6.0.0 nodes also read: they reject the flags with `unknown flag`.
  - Default allow lists are unaffected.

**Developers**

- **`[npm]` The packages require Node.js 24** ([#674](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/674)). `engines.node` is now `>=24`, up from `>=20.16`.
- **`[PXE]` The `resolveTaggingSecretStrategy` hook also decides self-sends** ([#608](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/608)).
  - The PXE used to replace the hook's answer with an address-derived secret when an account sent to itself.
  - `DEFAULT_TAGGING_SECRET_STRATEGY` is replaced by `defaultTaggingSecretStrategy(request)`.
  - To keep the old behaviour for self-sends, return it for messages your hook has no policy for:

  ```diff
   resolveTaggingSecretStrategy: async (request) =>
     knownContacts.has(request.recipient.toString())
       ? { type: 'address-derived' }
  -    : { type: 'non-interactive-handshake' },
  +    : defaultTaggingSecretStrategy(request),
  ```

- **`[PXE]` `generateSimulatedProvingResult` takes the transaction's max expiration timestamp and an options object** ([#600](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/600), [#601](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/601)):

  ```diff
  - await generateSimulatedProvingResult(result, getFunctionName, node, minRevertibleSideEffectCounter);
  + await generateSimulatedProvingResult(
  +   result,
  +   getFunctionName,
  +   node,
  +   await computeSimulatedMaxExpirationTimestamp(result, node),
  +   { minRevertibleSideEffectCounterOverride: minRevertibleSideEffectCounter },
  + );
  ```

- **`[Aztec.js]` A v6.1.0 app cannot parse `simulateTx` results with tagged logs from a v6.0.0 wallet** ([#620](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/620)). `AppTaggingSecret` now requires a `deliveryMode` field, which v6.0.0 writes as `kind`. Upgrade apps and wallets together.
- **`[Aztec.js]` `L1RollupConstants` no longer has `rollupManaLimit`** ([#546](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/546)). Governance can raise the limit at any time, so read it with `RollupContract.getManaLimit()`. The node's `getL1Constants` still returns the field, filled with the live value, but it is deprecated.
- **`[Noir tests]` Messages between `TestEnvironment` accounts follow the PXE's new default tagging** ([#608](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/608)). They now establish a non-interactive handshake instead of using an address-derived secret, unless you set a strategy with `with_default_tag_secret_strategy`.
- **`[CLI]` `aztec sequencers` is removed** ([#556](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/556)). Its replacements:
  - `aztec add-l1-validator` for deposits;
  - `aztec remove-l1-validator --recipient` for exits;
  - `aztec debug-rollup` for the registered validators and the current proposer.
- **`[Aztec.nr]` Contracts compiled with v6.1.0 need a v6.1.0 PXE for the new oracles.** Aztec.nr's oracle interface is now version 33.2 ([#550](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/550), [#621](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/621)).
  - A v6.0.0 PXE fails with `Oracle '…' not found … requires a newer private execution environment` when such a contract calls `get_tx_effects_with_block`, or sends a message with address-derived tagging.
  - Contracts compiled with v6.0.0 keep working on a v6.1.0 PXE.

## For node operators

**L1**

- **The node stops sending requests to L1 RPC URLs that fall behind** ([#587](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/587)).
  - With two or more URLs in `ETHEREUM_HOSTS`, the node checks each URL's latest block every few seconds. It sets aside a URL that falls behind or stops answering, and uses it again once it catches up. A URL on the wrong L1 chain is never used.
  - Look for `Demoted L1 RPC URL` and `Restored L1 RPC URL` in the logs.
  - Tuning (the defaults suit most setups): `ETHEREUM_HOSTS_GRADER_INTERVAL_MS` (4000), `_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS` (1000), `_MAX_BLOCKS_BEHIND` (2), `_THRESHOLD` (3), `_WINDOW` (5), `_KEEP_DEMOTED` (false).
- **Calls that come back `null` fail over to the next URL** ([#585](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/585)). Before, an unsynced first URL answering `null` for the latest block stalled L1 sync, even with a healthy second URL.
- **The L1 publisher treats "already known" as a successful send** ([#588](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/588)). It tracks each tx by the hash it computes locally, and resends a signed tx up to three times on timeouts, network errors, HTTP 408/429/5xx and rate limits.
- **New `L1_MINIMUM_PRIORITY_FEE_PER_GAS_FOR_CAP_GWEI` (default 0.001)** ([#563](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/563)). When the RPC estimates a zero priority fee, the publisher no longer drops its 100× sanity cap on the competitive fee; it caps against this floor instead.
- **The startup L1 logs check reads from the node's latest checkpoint** ([#683](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/683)).
  - Before, it asked for the rollup's deployment event, and a URL that pruned old logs had to be bypassed with `ARCHIVER_SKIP_HISTORICAL_LOGS_CHECK=true`. That is no longer needed with a recent snapshot.
  - A URL that answers with an error (including 4444 for pruned history) now only logs a warning.
  - Startup still fails on a URL that returns empty results for blocks it holds.
- **`trace_transaction` responses with `create` or `suicide` entries, or halted calls, parse correctly** ([#508](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/508)). The archiver used to fall back to `debug_traceTransaction` on these.
- **Consensus hosts that fail the startup probe are re-probed every 5 minutes** ([#576](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/576)). Before, they were dropped until the next restart.

**Governance changes and fees**

- **The node follows the rollup's live mana limit, mana target and proving cost** ([#546](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/546)). These were read once at startup. After a governance raise, a node that started earlier stopped syncing, withheld attestations from honest proposals and under-filled its own checkpoints, so it needed a restart. It now polls the rollup every second.
- **Gossip max-gas rejections around a mana-limit change no longer disconnect the relayer** ([#582](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/582)).
- **Validators check a checkpoint's opening block fees against L1** ([#517](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/517)).
  - New, non-slashable rejection reasons: `gas_fees_mismatch` and `gas_fees_unavailable`.
  - A run of `gas_fees_unavailable` points at your own L1 endpoint, not at the proposer.

**Provers**

- **Epochs an early proof already covered are proven in full** ([#693](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/693)). A partial proof that landed while its epoch was still open used to make the node skip that epoch, losing its reward share and activity score. Expect one extra proof submission for each such epoch. `PROVER_NODE_DISABLE_FULL_EPOCH_PROVING` still turns this off. Stopping a prover no longer waits out tx gathering.
- **`WS_HISTORY_RETENTION` must cover the proof submission window** ([#714](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/714)).
  - A prover now refuses to start with `rolling:N` below `(proofSubmissionEpochs + 1) × epochDuration`. That limit includes values set through the deprecated `WS_NUM_HISTORIC_*` variables. The error prints the minimum.
  - Left unset, a prover now defaults to that window (at least `rolling:64`) and logs the value.
- **Witness generation failures caused by the machine are retried** ([#532](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/532)). This covers OOM kills, spawn failures and OS file errors. Before, one failure sank the whole epoch.
- **Correct L1-to-L2 messages after an L1 reorg** ([#557](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/557)). The prover node checks a checkpoint's messages against its inbox rolling hash, so after a reorg it no longer captures a message list that can never prove the checkpoint.
- **Correct attestations after an L1 reorg** ([#549](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/549)). A checkpoint republished after a reorg now has its attestations refreshed, so the proof submits the bytes L1 stores.

**Slashing accuracy**

v6.1.0 fixes edge cases where honest nodes could report an innocent validator for slashing. It needs no action and changes nothing for nodes that behave correctly.

- **Attesters are reported only for what they signed.** Before, a bad proposal in the same slot ([#346](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/346)), or a proposer leaving one of its own blocks out of its checkpoint ([#525](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/525)), could get attesters reported for signing a valid checkpoint. Now only the misbehaving proposer is reported.
- **A local AVM crash no longer counts against the proposer** ([#530](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/530)). If your node's AVM process dies twice while checking a block (for example, out of memory), the node skips attesting with `simulator_failure` instead of reporting the block as invalid.
- **The data-withholding check matches the exact transactions collected** ([#702](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/702)).
- **New monitoring statuses** ([#362](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/362)): sentinel stats now split valid proposals that never reached L1 into two statuses. `checkpoint-unpublished` means the proposer had everything it needed and didn't land the checkpoint. `checkpoint-orphaned` means an earlier checkpoint it depended on never landed. Neither status affects slashing.

These fixes change which reports your own node makes, so they take full effect once most of the network has upgraded.

**Chain sync and proposals**

- **An invalid checkpoint on L1 no longer costs the honest proposals behind it** ([#527](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/527), [#529](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/529)).
- **The archiver reads rollup state at its sync round's L1 block** ([#552](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/552)). Before, a lagging RPC backend could make a rollback delete checkpoints still on L1, and lower the proven and finalized tips. The archiver also prunes evicted blocks' bodies with their headers ([#717](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/717)).
- **The checkpoint's final block arrives even if a copy without it came first** ([#518](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/518)).
- **Blob retrieval handles missed L1 slots** ([#559](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/559)).

**P2P and the tx pool**

- **A node that restarts at a new address is reachable again** ([#631](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/631)). The ENR sequence is seeded from the clock.
- **Bootnodes only accept and serve peers on the same L1 chain** ([#675](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/675)).
- **Relayers are not penalized for transactions that expired within the last slot** ([#480](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/480)).
- **The node no longer rejects transactions still valid at their expiration timestamp.** The rollup treats that timestamp as inclusive ([#600](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/600)).
- **Setup allow list admission matches what the AVM runs:**
  - setup calls resolve only against contracts deployed in the non-revertible half ([#705](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/705));
  - address entries require a deployed contract ([#706](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/706));
  - runtime changes to the allow list reach the tx pool ([#707](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/707)).

  `aztec_getAllowedPublicSetup` returns the new `minGas` field ([#701](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/701)).
- **RPC submissions need the configured price bump to evict a same-fee-payer tx for balance** ([#679](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/679)).

**Snapshots, blobs and operations**

- **Snapshot upload status through the admin API** ([#713](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/713)).
  - `aztecAdmin_startSnapshotUpload(location, operationId?)` accepts a caller-generated UUID.
  - Poll `aztecAdmin_getSnapshotUploadStatus(operationId)` for `capturing`, `uploading`, `succeeded` or `failed`.
  - One-argument calls still work.
- **Snapshot uploads retry transient object-store errors** ([#652](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/652)). An S3 HEAD that fails with anything but not-found or 403 no longer gets read as "no index yet", which used to overwrite `index.json` ([#685](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/685)).
- **Blob filestore uploads retry transient errors** ([#716](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/716)).
  - The node retries after 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16s.
  - A failing startup healthcheck no longer stops the node.
  - New metrics: `aztec.blob_client.upload_attempt_count`, `aztec.blob_client.upload_request_count` and `aztec.blob_client.upload_duration`. Alert on failed requests to detect gaps.
- **RPC method names in logs and traces** ([#676](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/676)). Behind a proxy that overwrites `x-aztec-client-id`, set `RPC_TRUST_CLIENT_ID_HEADER=true` (default false) to record the client ID too.
- **HA validators with an odd `VALIDATOR_HA_MAX_STUCK_DUTIES_AGE_MS` sign again** ([#669](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/669)). Every signing used to fail with a `RangeError`. The default was not affected.
- **The arm64 Docker image uses tcmalloc** ([#564](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/564)). It no longer prints an `ld.so` preload error on every exec.

## For developers

**Aztec.nr**

- **`get_tx_effects_with_block`** returns each settled transaction's effects with the block that included it ([#550](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/550)).
- **`NoteValidationRequest` is public**, exported from `aztec::messages::processing` with `owner()`, `storage_slot()`, `packed_note()` and `tx_hash()` accessors ([#535](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/535)).
- **A `DelayedPublicMutable` read sets the expiration timestamp one second earlier.** The rollup's expiration is inclusive ([#600](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/600)).
- **Deprecated:** `get_app_tagging_secret` → `get_app_address_derived_tagging_secret`, and `compute_app_siloed_shared_secret` → `compute_app_siloed_shared_secret_from_point` ([#620](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/620), [#621](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/621)).

**PXE**

- **`getPrivateEvents` returns each event's commitment randomness** (`PackedPrivateEvent.randomness`), so a user can disclose a single private event ([#618](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/618)). `BaseWallet.getPrivateEvents` is unchanged.
- **The `resolveExpirationAndPadding` hook** lets a wallet choose a transaction's expiration timestamp and its side-effect padding ([#601](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/601)). Without the hook, proving behaves as before.
- **Kernelless simulation reports the expiration the proven transaction publishes** ([#600](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/600)). It used to be up to an hour later.
- **Browser PXE stores survive interruptions:**
  - a reload mid-commit, which used to give `SQLITE_CORRUPT`; sqlite3mc is now 2.6.1, on SQLite 3.54.0 ([#578](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/578));
  - a navigation during the first open, which used to give `SQLITE_CANTOPEN` ([#551](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/551)).
- **Errors in PXE logs keep their message and stack** ([#599](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/599)).
- **Deprecated:** `appSiloEcdhSharedSecretPoint` → `computeAppSiloedSharedSecretFromPoint` ([#620](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/620)).

**Aztec.js**

- **`getAllPublicEvents`** returns every public event matching a block range or tx hash, oldest first ([#624](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/624)). The paged `getPublicEvents` is deprecated.
- **Wallet inputs have size limits** as part of the [security fix](#security):
  - most lists a dApp sends to the wallet are capped at 1,024 entries, and function arguments at 16,384 ([#638](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/638));
  - contract artifacts and ABIs are capped ([#639](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/639)).

  Valid input stays well within these limits.
- **An ephemeral browser `EmbeddedWallet` keeps its PXE data in memory** ([#571](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/571)). A second ephemeral wallet on the same page used to fail.
- **Published packages declare the dependencies they import** ([#728](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/728)). That fixes yarn's YN0086 warning, and `aztec-wallet deploy` and `register-contract` no longer depend on hoisting.

**CLI**

- **`aztec test`** no longer crashes when its output pipe fills up, and no longer hangs when the TXE dies. It fails up front if port 8081 is taken ([#592](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/592)).
- **`aztec-wallet bridge-fee-juice --wait`** keeps polling until the node has the claim message ([#741](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/741)). It used to give up on the first poll.
- **`aztec-up`'s bare `latest` and `nightly` aliases follow the v6 line** ([#560](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/560)). To pin the line explicitly, use `v6-latest`.

## Summary

v6 is the new Aztec rollup deployment proposed in [AZUP-3](https://forum.aztec.network/t/azup-3-is-ready-for-proposal/8670). It is a major protocol upgrade, and upgrading to v6.0.0 is required for everyone. The new rollup becomes canonical on Mainnet no earlier than **Monday 26 October 2026, 08:00 UTC**, and Testnet upgrades at the same time.

**Node operators: two breaking changes.** A trace-capable L1 endpoint is now required by default, and the Docker image moved to the `azteclabs` Docker Hub organization. See [Breaking changes for node operators](#breaking-changes-for-node-operators).

Almost everything you pull from has moved: the Docker image is now published under `azteclabs` (`azteclabs/aztec`), the npm packages are now under `@aztec-labs` and `@aztec-foundation`, and Aztec.nr is now published from `aztec-labs-eng/aztec-nr`.

## Breaking changes for node operators

- **A trace-capable L1 endpoint is required by default** ([#511](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/511)). `ETHEREUM_ALLOW_NO_DEBUG_HOSTS` now defaults to `false`: the node refuses to start unless `ETHEREUM_DEBUG_HOSTS` (or `ETHEREUM_HOSTS`) serves `debug_traceTransaction` or `trace_transaction`. Without traces, a node silently stops syncing at the first checkpoint published through a non-standard contract. Set the flag to `true` to accept that risk.
- **The Docker image moved to the `azteclabs` Docker Hub organization**: `azteclabs/aztec` (and `azteclabs/aztec-prover-agent`). The image name is unchanged, but `aztecprotocol/aztec` has no v6 releases; a compose file still pointing at it pulls v5.

  ```diff
  - image: aztecprotocol/aztec:5.2.0
  + image: azteclabs/aztec:6.0.0
  ```

## When to switch on Mainnet

**Option 1 (recommended): standby.** Start a v6 node next to your v5 node any time before the execution date. At startup it compares the canonical rollup's genesis archive root, VK tree root and protocol contracts hash with its own. While v5 is canonical they differ, so the node enters standby: it serves only a health endpoint (which reports healthy), checks L1 once a minute, and uses very few resources. When the v6 rollup becomes canonical it logs `Compatible rollup found` and starts normally, with nothing for you to do.

- Run it on a separate host, or give it its own container name, `AZTEC_PORT` and `P2P_PORT`. Standby binds the HTTP port as soon as it starts, and the node binds the P2P port when it leaves standby, so reusing the v5 values makes it fail.
- Use a new, empty data directory.
- Leave `ROLLUP_VERSION` unset so the node follows the canonical rollup. Pinning it to the v6 rollup's version makes the node fail at startup, because that version is not in the registry until the proposal executes.
- Keep your v5 node running until the v6 node has left standby and is attesting.

**Option 2: upgrade at execution time.** Stop the v5 node and start v6 on Monday 26 October 2026 at 08:00 UTC, or as soon after as the proposal executes. Your sequencer is idle until the v6 node has started and synced. Slashing is disabled for the first 8,400 slots (about 7 days) after the v6 rollup becomes canonical, so the slots you miss while starting up cost you rewards but do not get you slashed.

**High-availability signing on a shared PostgreSQL database:** v5 nodes delete other rollups' signing records when they start ([#352](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/352) fixes this in v6 only). Give your v6 replicas their own database, or do not restart v5 replicas after the switch, so the v6 replicas keep their double-signing protection.

Full operator migration guide: [v6.0.0 operator changelog](https://docs.aztec.network/operate/operators/reference/changelog/v6).

## Breaking changes

Everything below applies to every project moving from v5.2.0.

**Where things live**

- **`[Docker]` The image moved to the `azteclabs` Docker Hub organization**: `azteclabs/aztec` (and `azteclabs/aztec-prover-agent`). `aztecprotocol/aztec` has no v6 releases; a compose file still pointing at it pulls v5.

  ```diff
  - image: aztecprotocol/aztec:5.2.0
  + image: azteclabs/aztec:6.0.0
  ```

- **`[npm]` Packages moved to `@aztec-labs`** ([#93](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/93)), and the foundation packages (`bb.js`, the `noir-*` packages, `l1-artifacts`, and others) to **`@aztec-foundation`** ([#113](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/113)). Subpaths are unchanged beyond the scope. The `@aztec` scope keeps everything already published, so v5 projects keep installing.

  ```diff
  -import { Contract } from '@aztec/aztec.js';
  +import { Contract } from '@aztec-labs/aztec.js';
  ```

- **`[npm]` The packages depend on upstream `viem`**, not the `@aztec/viem` fork ([#304](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/304)). If you aliased `viem` to the fork, depend on upstream `viem` at the version `@aztec-labs/aztec.js` uses.
- **`[Aztec.nr]` Aztec.nr is published from `aztec-labs-eng/aztec-nr`.** `AztecProtocol/aztec-nr` has no v6 tags, so bumping only `tag` fails with `Remote branch v6.x.x not found`. Update `git` as well ([#135](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/135)):

  ```diff
  -aztec = { git = "https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-nr", tag = "v5.2.0", directory = "aztec" }
  +aztec = { git = "https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-nr", tag = "v6.0.0", directory = "aztec" }
  ```

- **`[Aztec.nr]` The ECDSA note and the protocol contract interfaces ship with aztec-nr** ([#404](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/404)). Depend on them from `aztec-labs-eng/aztec-nr` at the same tag as `aztec`. Pulling them from the old repositories brings in a second copy of `aztec` and fails with `No matching impl found`.

**Protocol: every address changes, every contract recompiles**

- **The contract address domain separator is bumped to V3**, so every contract address, account addresses included, differs from v5 for the same class, salt, initialization and keys. This is deliberate: an address can never be live on two rollups at once. Anything that hard-codes an address must be updated. Protocol contracts keep their magic addresses (`1`, `2`, ...).
- **Block headers commit to a per-block tx effects tree** ([#123](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/123)). A block header alone now proves a transaction's inclusion and exact effects with a short membership proof. Every transaction hash, verification key, contract artifact and canonical address changes with it.
- **The protocol nullifier is derived from the tx request's salt alone** ([#310](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/310)). Two transactions with the same origin and salt (a fee bump or a cancellation) are mutually exclusive: at most one is mined. `tx_request_salt` in the private context becomes `protocol_nullifier`. **Wallets must draw a fresh salt for every transaction.** Contracts need only a recompile.
- **The standard contracts are at new addresses.** `MultiCallEntrypoint`, `HandshakeRegistry`, `AuthRegistry` and `PublicChecks` are all re-pinned. Handshakes made with the v5 registry must be re-established.
- **The PXE oracle interface is now version 33.** Contracts must be recompiled against Aztec.nr v6.0.0 to run against a v6 PXE.

**Aztec.nr**

- **Fact collections are scoped by `FactScope`** instead of an `AztecAddress` ([#426](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/426)). `FactScope::account(address)` is the old behaviour; the new `FactScope::public()` is shared by all accounts.

  ```diff
  - record_retractable_fact(contract_address, recipient, type_id, collection_id, fact_type_id, payload, origin_block);
  + record_retractable_fact(contract_address, FactScope::account(recipient), type_id, collection_id, fact_type_id, payload, origin_block);
  ```

- **`OriginBlock` is replaced by `aztec::oracle::block_reference::BlockReference`**, with the same fields ([#157](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/157)).
- **Nullifier existence checks are batched**: `get_nullifier_statuses` checks any number of nullifiers in one oracle call and reports each one's inclusion block. `check_nullifier_exists` still works ([#157](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/157)).
- **`Writer::advance_offset` is removed.** Serialize the skipped fields instead ([#387](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/387)).
- **`DelayedPublicMutable` rejects delays below one hour**, at compile time for the initial delay and at runtime in `schedule_delay_change` ([#99](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/99)).
- **Nine `DOM_SEP__*` constants left the protocol constants module.** `DOM_SEP__PARTIAL_NOTE_COMMITMENT` and `DOM_SEP__NOTE_COMPLETION_LOG_TAG` move to `aztec::note::partial_note`; the other seven are now internal. Custom account entrypoints should call `compute_tx_nullifier` instead of hashing `DOM_SEP__TX_NULLIFIER` themselves ([AztecProtocol/aztec-packages#25014](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25014)).

**Aztec.js**

- **Protocol contract wrappers moved to `@aztec-labs/aztec.js/protocol`** and out of `@aztec-labs/noir-contracts.js`. They are bound to their canonical address, so they attach with `withWallet(wallet)`. `at(wallet)` still works but is deprecated ([AztecProtocol/aztec-packages#24998](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24998)).

  ```diff
  - import { FeeJuiceContract } from '@aztec/noir-contracts.js/FeeJuice';
  + import { FeeJuiceContract } from '@aztec-labs/aztec.js/protocol';
  - const feeJuice = FeeJuiceContract.at(ProtocolContractAddress.FeeJuice, wallet);
  + const feeJuice = FeeJuiceContract.withWallet(wallet);
  ```

- **A function's return type is a single `returnType`**, not a `returnTypes` list. `decodeFromAbi` takes one type; use `decodeEachFromAbi` for lists ([AztecProtocol/aztec-packages#25066](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25066)).
- **Artifacts keep the names of `#[abi(tag)]` globals**, readable with `getGlobalsByTag`. Artifacts compiled before this are rejected and must be recompiled ([AztecProtocol/aztec-packages#25184](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25184)).
- **`GasPrice` is renamed `FeesPerGas`** in `@aztec-labs/ethereum/l1-tx-utils`, with matching method and field renames (`getGasPrice()` → `getFeesPerGas()`) ([AztecProtocol/aztec-packages#25152](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25152)).

**Node API**

- **`getBlockHashMembershipWitness` requires a reference block the node has.** v5 accepted a block number one past the tip; v6 does not. To prove against a specific archive root, including a block's own post-block archive, use the new `getBlockHashMembershipWitnessAtArchive({ archive }, blockHash)` ([#334](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/334)).

**CLI**

- **Removed `aztec bridge-erc20`.** Use `L1ToL2TokenPortalManager` from `@aztec-labs/aztec.js/ethereum`. Fee juice bridging with `aztec-wallet bridge-fee-juice` is unchanged ([#52](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/52)).
- **Removed `get-canonical-sponsored-fpc-address`.** `aztec-wallet` now aliases it as `contracts:SponsoredFPC` ([#49](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/49)).
- **Removed `inspect-contract`, `compute-selector`, `generate-secret-and-hash`, `parse-parameter-struct` and `example-contracts`.** Their aztec.js equivalents are listed in the migration notes ([#36](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/36)).

**Node operators**

- **`ACVM_*` is renamed `NOIR_EXECUTE_*`, with no fallback** ([#116](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/116)). A prover agent exits with `Requested real proving but no path to bb or noir-execute binaries provided`; a node not doing real proofs starts anyway but falls back to much slower WASM simulation.

  ```diff
  - ACVM_BINARY_PATH=/usr/src/labs-aztec-toolchain/bin/noir-execute
  - ACVM_WORKING_DIRECTORY=/usr/src/acvm
  + NOIR_EXECUTE_BINARY_PATH=/usr/src/labs-aztec-toolchain/bin/noir-execute
  + NOIR_EXECUTE_WORKING_DIRECTORY=/usr/src/noir-execute
  ```

  The same rename applies to the `--sequencer.*` and `--proverNode.*` flags. The release image sets the new variables itself.

## For node operators

**Attester-initiated sequencer exits** ([#215](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/215))

A position can now be exited by its attester, not only its withdrawer, and exits can be batched: each attester signs an authorization offline, and one relayer submits them all in one transaction. This is built for staking providers, who hold the attester keys for many delegations but not the withdrawer keys.

```bash
# 1. Each attester signs an exit authorization (offline), appended to one file
aztec sign-attester-exit --private-key $ATTESTER_KEY --attester $ATTESTER \
    --rollup $ROLLUP --l1-chain-id $L1_CHAIN_ID --deadline $DEADLINE \
    --output exits.json --append

# 2. Simulate, then submit from any funded key
aztec initiate-withdraw-by-attester-batch --dry-run --authorizations exits.json \
    --rollup $ROLLUP --l1-chain-id $L1_CHAIN_ID --l1-rpc-urls $L1_RPC
aztec initiate-withdraw-by-attester-batch --authorizations exits.json \
    --rollup $ROLLUP --l1-chain-id $L1_CHAIN_ID --l1-rpc-urls $L1_RPC \
    --private-key $RELAYER_KEY

# 3. The withdrawer names the recipient (does not restart the delay)
aztec remove-l1-validator --validator $ATTESTER --recipient $RECIPIENT \
    --rollup $ROLLUP --l1-rpc-urls $L1_RPC --l1-chain-id $L1_CHAIN_ID \
    --private-key $WITHDRAWER_KEY

# 4. After the delay, anyone finalizes
cast send $ROLLUP "finalizeWithdraw(address)" $ATTESTER --private-key $ANY_KEY --rpc-url $L1_RPC
```

What to know:

- **The stake always goes to the withdrawer's chosen recipient, never to the attester.** If you are a provider exiting delegated positions, your delegators must do step 3.
- **Timing.** On Mainnet the stake is claimable about 9.6 days after the exit starts: the rollup's 4-day exit delay and the 9.6-day governance withdrawal delay both have to pass.
- **Rate limit.** At most `floor((N - 1) / 20)` attester-initiated exits (about 5% of the set) per rolling 9.6-day window, never taking the set below the 48-seat committee. Withdrawer exits are not limited. Check the current state with `getAttesterExitLimitState()`.
- **Batches.** By default a batch is all or nothing against the rate limit; `--up-to-limit` processes as many as fit and leaves the rest for later. Either way, one invalid entry (expired deadline, bad signature, already exiting) reverts the whole transaction, so always `--dry-run` first.
- **Only on the canonical rollup.** On Mainnet, attester exits work on v6 once the upgrade executes, not on v5. Until then, pass the v6 rollup to `sign-attester-exit` with `--rollup` explicitly.
- `aztec initiate-withdraw-by-attester` exits one position in a transaction sent from the attester key.
- **`aztec remove-l1-validator` and `aztec sequencers remove` now require `--recipient`** ([#520](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/520)). Both used to make the attester's own address the recipient, which sent the stake to the hot attester key (or, for delegated stake, to the provider) and could not be changed afterwards. `remove-l1-validator --recipient`, run by the withdrawer, is also how you name the recipient after an attester-initiated exit.

Full guide: [Exiting a sequencer](https://docs.aztec.network/operate/operators/sequencer-management/exiting-a-sequencer).

**Publishers and L1**

- **Nodes check that a publisher can afford its L1 transaction before doing the work** ([#443](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/443)). A sequencer with no funded publisher skips the slot before building anything; a prover finishes the proof but holds it back, retrying every 12 seconds until a publisher is funded or the submission window closes. A dust-funded idle publisher can no longer win every proposal.
- **Publisher balances are checked every minute, for every publisher** ([#465](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/465), [#466](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/466)). The node logs which publisher to fund and how much ETH it is missing. New metrics `aztec_l1_publisher_sends_affordable`, `aztec_l1_publisher_required_balance_eth` and `aztec_l1_publisher_funder_balance_eth`; `aztec_l1_publisher_balance_eth` is now always recorded, and `aztec_l1_balance_eth` is deprecated. Alert on `aztec_l1_publisher_sends_affordable < 1`.
- **A clear error and metric when the L1 RPC cannot trace a propose transaction** ([#509](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/509)).
- **Proof submissions that run out of gas are resent** ([#491](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/491)), and very early epoch proofs are resubmitted correctly ([#397](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/397)).

**BLS keys and staking**

- **The upgrade raises the GSE's proof-of-possession gas cap from 250k to 300k.** Since Osaka's modexp repricing, about 1 in 28,600 honestly generated BLS keys needed more than 250k gas to verify, and their deposits were refunded and dropped from the entry queue. At 300k that is about 1 in 2.5 million. The GSE is shared, so this also applies to v5 from the moment the upgrade executes.
- **`aztec validator-keys` and the staker output now check BLS keys against the live cap**, so you find an expensive key before depositing it ([#396](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/396), [#507](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/507)).

**Provers**

- **New: `PROVER_NODE_DISABLE_FULL_EPOCH_PROVING`** ([#436](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/436)). When `true`, the prover node stops proving complete epochs on its own and proves only the partial epochs requested through its `startProof` admin method. Use it to serve paid partial-epoch proofs (for example, for early withdrawals) without competing for full epoch proofs. Default `false`.
- **Fault recovery.** A dead batch verifier is rebuilt ([#359](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/359), [#354](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/354)), prover agents report preemption ([#475](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/475)) and finish their proof on shutdown ([#300](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/300)), and per-block L1-to-L2 messages are capped when slicing checkpoints ([#390](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/390)).

**Operations**

- **Change the log level without a restart** ([#497](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/497)). `aztecAdmin_setConfig` accepts a `logLevel` in the `LOG_LEVEL` format (e.g. `"debug;trace:sequencer,p2p"`), and `aztecAdmin_getConfig` reports it. A restart reverts to `LOG_LEVEL`.
- **The node exits when its world state database process dies**, instead of running on without it, including on an idle node at genesis ([#449](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/449), [#460](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/460)).
- **HA signing keeps each rollup's signing history** across restarts of replicas serving other rollups, with a 24-hour default retention set by `VALIDATOR_HA_OLD_DUTIES_MAX_AGE_H` ([#352](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/352)). See the warning under [When to switch on Mainnet](#when-to-switch-on-mainnet).
- **New node RPC methods:** `aztec_getTxEffectMembershipWitness` and `aztec_getValidatorStatsBatch`.

## For wallet / PXE developers

- **Draw a fresh salt for every transaction.** Transactions with the same origin and salt now share a protocol nullifier, so at most one is mined. This is what makes fee bumps and cancellations possible, and it means a reused salt silently drops a transaction ([#310](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/310)).
- **PXE databases re-initialize on first open** (data schema bump), and the PXE requires contracts built against oracle interface version 33.
- **Tx inclusion proofs from a block header.** `TxEffect.computeTxEffectLeaf()`, `Body.computeTxEffectsTreeRoot()` and the node's `aztec_getTxEffectMembershipWitness` prove that a transaction was included in a block with exactly a given set of effects ([#123](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/123)).
- **Browser-facing packages no longer import Node.js-specific modules** ([#444](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/444)).

## Security & correctness

Most of this is in how the node treats input from peers and from L1.

- **p2p:** gossip messages with trailing bytes are rejected ([#236](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/236)); tx req/resp requests are de-duplicated, capped and bounded ([#201](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/201), [#202](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/202), [#379](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/379)); public calldata and contract class log validation are tighter ([#510](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/510)); a tx whose proof was evicted is dropped rather than served without it ([#375](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/375)); and peers are no longer penalized for conditions that are local to the receiver ([#143](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/143), [#235](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/235), [#316](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/316), [#477](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/477)).
- **Archiver:** checkpoints that repeat a tx hash are rejected ([#338](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/338)); a rolled-back checkpoint range re-syncs at the same L1 head ([#381](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/381)); a failed batch restores the L1 sync point ([#336](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/336)); and a checkpoint accepted earlier in the same batch is a valid parent ([#503](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/503)).
- **Slashing accuracy:** checkpoint proposals with a forged `lastArchiveRoot` are slashable ([#339](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/339)); proposals rejected only because of a reorg during validation are not ([#315](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/315)); equivocation is slashed only when one key signed both checkpoints ([#493](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/493)); and a committee is served only once its seed is fixed on L1 ([#500](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/500)).

## New in this release

- **Attester-initiated, batched sequencer exits.** See [For node operators](#for-node-operators).
- **Public fact collections.** `FactScope::public()` lets any execution of a contract read and write a collection, whichever accounts are in scope ([#426](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/426)).
- **Deployment framework:** universal deploys ([#16](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/16)) and deployment transactions paid through a payment method you supply ([#455](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/455)).
- **`getBlockHashMembershipWitnessAtArchive`** proves block membership against any archive root the node knows ([#334](https://github.com/aztec-labs-eng/aztec-node/pull/334)).

## Protocol constants

New in v6. The Mainnet v6 rollup ([`0xE37A2663Cc9c119BA41572C40fAb0bbb23a5402f`](https://etherscan.io/address/0xE37A2663Cc9c119BA41572C40fAb0bbb23a5402f), rollup version `2070860440`) was deployed with:

```
vk root               0x22fff5de6ce590153df4468f7f0b152188a803d91b3c9c648b91d93d5913f219
protocol contracts    0x0f54271c52865841a77aaa66036eed901aff22fdce9f08e123ec8b205c9854d7
genesis archive root  0x29eb2c527f8d45276430363214e6c8d709ef3f657a3670ebac3179373d41e5c4
```

A v6.0.0 node starts only when the canonical rollup carries exactly these values, which is what makes standby mode safe: it cannot attach to the wrong rollup. The new Testnet rollup uses the same circuits.

## Before you start

- **New Docker image name.** The image moved from `aztecprotocol/aztec` to **`azteclabs/aztec`**. The old repository has no v6 releases.
- **Use a fresh data directory.** v6 is a new rollup and syncs from its own genesis. v5 state doesn't carry over.
- **L1 RPC history.** Your L1 execution RPC must serve `eth_getLogs` back to the v6 Inbox deployment block.
